page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.96xlarge is a compute-focused high-performance computing instance designed for demanding tightly coupled parallel workloads. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance runs on the x86_64 architecture with AMD EPYC 9R14 processors operating at 3.7 GHz. It provides 192 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio, eliminating resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 768.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 300 Gbps baseline network bandwidth to handle intense inter-node communication, while bundling zero local storage and no hardware GPUs.

Benchmark measurements reflect the dense multi-threaded architecture of the platform. Synthetic testing demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute capability, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 589,691.63 and PassMark CPU reaching 148,817.56. Heavy integer and floating-point tasks perform exceptionally well, marked by top-decile Geekbench results in software compilation (74,809.0) and ray tracing (189,252.0). Sustained uncached read memory bandwidth reaches 704.22 GB/sec, while write operations maintain 345.83 GB/sec. LLM inference results show strong prompt processing across small, medium, and large models due to core density and memory throughput, though text generation speed remains modest without dedicated GPU acceleration.

From an infrastructure perspective, the hpc7a.96xlarge achieves high efficiency for compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-dependent workloads by dedicating full physical cores rather than shared virtual threads. The trade-off is the total reliance on external network-attached storage, as the absence of local NVMe disks requires architecting storage over the 300 Gbps fabric. This profile fits computational fluid dynamics, weather modeling, molecular dynamics, distributed finite element analysis, and large-scale parallel software compilation.
